\chapter{Communication Complexity — Newman Theorem}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem
\section{Overview}

This module establishes Newman's theorem: every public-coin communication protocol
can be converted into a private-coin protocol with only $O(\log(|X| \cdot |Y|) / \varepsilon^2)$
additional bits of communication. The key construction is the \emph{Newman protocol}, which has
Alice sample a random index into a fixed table of good random seeds (chosen via a Chernoff
and union-bound argument) and send that index to Bob, after which both parties simulate the
original public-coin protocol deterministically.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Newman index space]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.newmanIndexSpace}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{pdf-d54d402b16e2-p012-b002}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p005-b004}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.newmanIndexSpace}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.derandomizationSamples}
Given finite input types $X$ and $Y$ and parameters $\varepsilon, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
the \emph{Newman index space} is $\mathrm{Fin}(\mathtt{derandomizationSamples}\;X\;Y\;\varepsilon\;c)$,
i.e.\ the finite type indexing the table of random seeds that Alice samples from in the Newman
reduction.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Newman protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.newmanProtocol}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{pdf-d54d402b16e2-p012-b002}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p005-b004}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.newmanProtocol}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toPrivateCoin, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.alice, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.exists_good_randomness, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toDeterministic, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.newmanIndexSpace}
Given a public-coin finite-message protocol $p$ over a probability space $\Omega$ that
$\varepsilon$-computes $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and a constant $c > 1$, the Newman protocol
is a private-coin finite-message protocol in which Alice draws a random index $i$ from
$\mathtt{newmanIndexSpace}\;X\;Y\;\varepsilon\;c$ and sends it to Bob; both players then
run the $i$-th seed from a fixed table of good randomness values (obtained via a Chernoff
and union-bound argument) through the original public-coin protocol deterministically.
\end{definition}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.comap_run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_prod, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.alice, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.rrun, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.exists_good_randomness, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.newmanProtocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.newmanIndexSpace, CommunicationComplexity.uniformOn_univ_measureReal_eq_card_filter}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, let $X$ and $Y$ be finite types, and let $p$
be a public-coin finite-message protocol over shared randomness $\Omega$ with inputs in
$X$ and $Y$ and outputs in a type $\alpha$. Fix a target function $f : X \times Y \to
\alpha$, a real error bound $\varepsilon$, and a real constant $c > 1$, and suppose that
$p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$, meaning that for every input pair $(x,y)$ the
probability over the shared randomness that $p$ outputs something other than $f(x,y)$ is
at most $\varepsilon$. Then the associated Newman protocol — the private-coin protocol
in which Alice draws an index into the fixed table of good random seeds, sends it to
Bob, and both run $p$ deterministically on that seed — $(c\varepsilon)$-computes $f$:
for every input pair $(x,y)$ the probability over the private randomness that its output
differs from $f(x,y)$ is at most $c\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toPrivateCoin_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.alice, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.derandomizationSamples, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.newmanProtocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toDeterministic_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.newmanIndexSpace}
\difficulty{3}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite types, let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $p$
be a public-coin finite-message protocol over $\Omega$ with private inputs in $X$ and
$Y$ and outputs in a type $\alpha$. Fix a target function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, real
parameters $\varepsilon$ and $c$ with $c > 1$, and suppose that $p$
$\varepsilon$-computes $f$. Then the communication complexity of the associated Newman
protocol equals
\[
  \left\lceil \log_2 t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c) \right\rceil + \mathrm{complexity}(p),
\]
where $t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c)$ is the derandomization sample count and
$\mathrm{complexity}(p)$ is the communication complexity of $p$; that is, running the
Newman protocol costs exactly the cost of $p$ together with the number of bits Alice
needs to name one seed in the table of size $t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Newman's theorem for communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.newman}
\proofsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p012-b002,
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p011-b005
}
\proofsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{
  pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p005-b003,
  pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p005-b004
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.newman}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ofProtocol_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ofProtocol_run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PrivateCoin.communicationComplexity_le_of_finiteMessage, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.derandomizationSamples, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.newmanProtocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.newmanProtocol_ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.newmanProtocol_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ofProtocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.rrun, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite types, let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and let $\varepsilon,
\varepsilon', c \in \bbr$ satisfy $1 < c$ and $c\varepsilon < \varepsilon'$. Then the
private-coin communication complexity of $f$ at error tolerance $\varepsilon'$ does not
exceed the public-coin communication complexity of $f$ at error tolerance $\varepsilon$
increased by $\lceil \log_2 t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c)\rceil$, where $t(X, Y, \varepsilon,
c)$ is the derandomization sample count; that is,
\[
  \mathrm{CC}^{\mathrm{priv}}_{\varepsilon'}(f)
  \;\le\;
  \mathrm{CC}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon}(f)
  \;+\;
  \bigl\lceil \log_2 t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c) \bigr\rceil ,
\]
with both complexities taken as values in $\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$.
\end{theorem}
